title: SignNow alternative: e-signature without per-seat pricing
author: Cryptool
excerpt_html: SignNow competes on price, and it is genuinely cheaper than DocuSign. Free is still cheaper, and encryption is the part the price comparison misses.
content_html:
SignNow's whole pitch is that it does most of what DocuSign does for a fraction of the price, and that pitch is basically true. It is the value option in e-signature, and teams that pick it are usually making a deliberate cost decision rather than a feature one. So a comparison against it has to be about price first, honestly, and then about the thing price does not cover. DocSign is free with a Cryptool account, and it encrypts documents so the platform cannot read them.

What SignNow does well

It is the cheapest credible name in the category, and it does not feel like a budget product. Unlimited sending on its paid tiers, a reasonable API, bulk send, and templates. If your requirement is straightforward e-signature at low cost from an established vendor, SignNow answers it and it has been doing so for years.

Where the comparison gets interesting

Price is a moving target and we are not going to publish SignNow's current numbers here, because they change and a stale figure is worse than none. What does not change is the shape: SignNow bills per user per month, billed annually, with the cheapest tier limited enough that most teams move up one. DocSign has no seat charge at all, because it is included with a Cryptool account.

The more substantive difference is what the vendor can read. On SignNow, as on DocuSign and Adobe, your executed documents sit in the vendor's cloud in readable form. That is the industry norm and it is not a scandal. It is simply a different answer to the question of who can see a term sheet, and for a crypto team it is often the wrong one.

What DocSign does differently

No seat pricing, because there is no pricing. It is free with a Cryptool account, so the finance question does not recur every year.

Client-side encryption. The document is encrypted in your browser, the key is wrapped to your account key, and the server holds only ciphertext. The caveat, stated plainly: an encrypted document cannot be shared with workspace members, because the uploader alone holds the key.

Sovereign mode. The PDF never leaves your device, only a fingerprint is stored, and the signed copy is emailed rather than retained. This is the option a storage-based vendor cannot match.

Hash-chain audit trail. Every event links to the one before it, so tampering after the fact breaks verification downstream. Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof, and the distinction is deliberate.

Optional signer verification. An emailed one-time code per envelope, when the document warrants it.

Choosing between them

If you want an established standalone vendor with a long track record and an API, and you are comfortable with the standard storage model, SignNow is a perfectly good choice at a fair price. If you are already using Cryptool, DocSign removes the cost entirely and adds encryption that the cheaper-vendor comparison does not address. The real question is not which is cheaper, since free wins that, but whether you want your signing tool inside the platform where the rest of your deal already lives.

Common questions

Is DocSign free, or is it a limited free tier?

Free with a Cryptool account, with no per-envelope or per-seat charge. It is one of the apps included with the account.

What is the catch?

DocSign is younger than SignNow and does not carry audited compliance certifications. If your counterparty requires a vendor with those certifications, that is a real reason to use an established name instead, and we would rather say so here than have you find out later.

Can I send the same document to many signers at once?

Yes. You can send in parallel or set a sequential order, and each signer gets their own share link.

Does DocSign store my signed documents?

By default yes, encrypted. In sovereign mode it does not: only a fingerprint is kept and the signed copy is emailed to you. You choose per document.

How do I try it?

Open DocSign with your Cryptool account.
